cf.title: Discard aborted updaters when expanding a multixact

input.subject: [PATCH] Discard aborted updaters when expanding a multixact

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The thread states the problem with a concrete interleaving, an independent pgbench reproducer on released versions (message #7) and a 2022 report with the same error. The fix changes existing conflict checks in heapam.c and adds no new user-visible surface. Confidence is medium because the code and the final commit were not read.

brief.title: Fix aborted multixact updater checks in heap update paths
brief.problem: Concurrent updates fail with "new multixact has more than one updating member" when an updater has recorded its abort in pg_xact but is still in ProcArray. A crashed updater without an abort record also causes a spurious TM_Updated after recovery when a prepared key-share locker survives. Users with high-concurrency workloads that combine FK locks and rolled-back updates hit this.
brief.proposed_design: The conflict check in heapam.c ignores a multixact updater only after it is no longer running and did not commit, so conflicting requests wait for the abort to finish. heap_update() then judges a finished updater by whether TransactionIdDidCommit() returns false instead of by TransactionIdDidAbort(). The v1 change to MultiXactIdExpand() was dropped in v3; v5 is Heikki's rewrite of the comments.
user_visible_surface: New injection point in xact.c after the abort is written to pg_xact and before ProcArray cleanup (test use).
author_claims: Removes the two-updater error without changing MultiXactIdExpand(); its existing filter discards the aborted member once the conflicting request has waited.
Fixes a spurious serialization error at REPEATABLE READ and a tmfd.traversed assertion at READ COMMITTED for crashed updaters.
heap_lock_updated_tuple_rec() can lock a dead successor and write extra WAL, but the author found no user-visible issue and left it unchanged.
Lionel Hamayon reports 43 of 48 pgbench clients failing within 30 seconds on REL_18_STABLE, and no errors in about 16 million transactions with v5.
Released versions 18.1 and 18.4 are affected; a 2022 report on 14.5 shows the same error.
brief.thread_state: Heikki reviewed, rewrote the comments as v5, and reports he committed and back-patched it to all supported versions on 2026-10-15. The CommitFest entry still shows Needs review.
unclear: The material does not show the final v5 commit message or which branches received which parts.
No measurement of extra waiting caused by conflicting requests now blocking until ProcArray cleanup.
Whether the new tests went into back branches is not stated.

questions: Which branches received the injection point in xact.c and the new isolation and recovery tests?
Is there a measurement of the extra wait for conflicting requests between the pg_xact abort write and ProcArray cleanup under high concurrency?
Should heap_lock_updated_tuple_rec() also test that TransactionIdDidCommit() returns false, so that it does not lock a dead successor of a crashed updater?
Does the CommitFest entry need its status changed from Needs review to Committed?

committability.owner_note: Heikki Linnakangas is reviewer and committer on the CommitFest entry, rewrote the comments as v5, and reports the commit and back-patch in the thread.
committability.liability: The committer signs for the changed conflict and updater-status checks in heapam.c on all supported branches, including any later lock-wait or visibility reports from that code.
committability.author_follow_up: The author rebased twice, widened the fix in v3 after finding the crashed-updater case, and audited related TransactionIdDidAbort() calls.

priority.reason: The bug hits workloads that mix foreign-key locks and rolled-back updates, with 43 of 48 pgbench clients failing in the report on REL_18_STABLE. The code patches are small and add no new surface, but the heapam.c multixact logic needs a reviewer who knows it.

provisional_note: The code and the final commit were not read, so the claim that every caller of the changed conflict check tolerates the added wait is unverified. The remaining TransactionIdDidAbort() use in heap_lock_updated_tuple_rec() rests on the author's analysis in message #3.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make VACUUM remove MultiXacts with updater XIDs more eagerly
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes FreezeMultiXactId() so that VACUUM removes a MultiXact outright when all of its members are older than OldestXmin, instead of leaving it in place with FRM_NOOP processing. The goal is to get more use out of each GetMultiXactIdMembers() call and to remove more Multis that have updater XIDs, since OldestMxact can be held back much longer than OldestXmin.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread ends when Peter Geoghegan creates the CF entry. No message shows a reviewer objecting to this patch or the author explaining the withdrawal. Andres Freund's objections in the thread concern the separate patch that skips the TransactionIdDidCommit() sanity checks.

precedents_retrieved.title: Skip collecting decoded changes of already-aborted transactions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Logical decoding checks CLOG when it first decodes a transaction and stops collecting decoded changes for transactions already known to be aborted, so large aborted transactions are not decoded again after a restart or lag. After Andres Freund's review, the revised patch checks transaction status only for large transactions at eviction time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The revised patch did not compile because `logical_replication_mode` was undeclared in `ReorderBufferCheckTXNAbort`. The author posted no new version after this report, so the CF manager returned the entry with feedback. Andres Freund's earlier concerns, misuse of TransactionIdDidAbort() and slow CLOG lookups, were addressed in the design but not decisive.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
With no update to the thread and the compilation still failing I'm
marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Lock updated tuples in tuple_update() and tuple_delete()
precedents_retrieved.summary: When tuple_update() or tuple_delete() finds a concurrently updated tuple in read committed mode, the table AM locks the updated version itself instead of returning TM_Updated for a separate tuple_lock() call. Later versions also had update and delete return the old tuple through a slot passed by the executor, which avoids refetching it and helps table AMs with costly TID lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Version 15 was committed in March 2023, then reverted after Andres Freund's post-commit review. He showed that RETURNING could use the wrong tuple, with an isolation test that fails. He also criticised the new API: the ignored wait parameter, tmfd turned into an input, and the LazyTupleTableSlot code. The redesigned old-tuple API came days before the version 16 feature freeze, and he said it was not ready for 16. In March 2024 the author planned to push a revised version, and the visible messages do not show why the entry was finally returned with feedback in October 2024.
matched_queries: key share lock update abort race
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I guess this really is part of my issue with this change - it optimizes the rare case, while not addressing the same inefficiency in the common case.

precedents_retrieved.title: POC: Lock updated tuples in tuple_update() and tuple_delete()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes tuple_update() and tuple_delete() lock a concurrently updated tuple as soon as they detect it, so a separate tuple_lock() call before the read committed recheck is no longer needed. It also simplifies nodeModifyTable.c and removes an extra table_tuple_fetch_row_version() call in ExecUpdate.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message, from the author on 2022-07-29, said a benchmark showed a small, noisy gain and that he would bring the patch into a more acceptable shape. No later message appears before the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow tuple visibility checks without hint-bit maintenance
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds HeapTupleSatisfiesVisibilityNoHints() and HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdateNoHints(), which return the normal visibility verdict without setting hint bits on the buffer. It targets table AMs that store heap-format tuples on pages logged through generic WAL, where an unlogged hint-bit write changes the page that a later generic WAL delta is computed against.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund asked why Postgres should support such an AM, since the patch did not explain its purpose. He also said the extra branches in performance-critical visibility code can slow it down, and that code with no in-tree users tends to bit-rot. The author replied that these comments led him to revisit the design, and he withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Why do we care about such an AM? What's the point of all of this?

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow tuple visibility checks without hint-bit, maintenance
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds HeapTupleSatisfiesVisibilityNoHints() and HeapTupleSatisfiesUpdateNoHints(), which return the normal visibility verdict without writing hint bits to the page. It targets table AMs that store heap-format tuples on pages logged with generic WAL, where an unlogged hint-bit write changes the before-image of the next delta.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the author withdrew it. The entry was withdrawn the day after posting, and shihao zhong withdrew a duplicate entry (7215) in favor of 7212, which may be this record. Andres Freund objected that the patch has no in-tree user and so may bit-rot, that it adds branches to performance-critical code, and that it does not explain why such an AM matters. shihao zhong questioned the corruption claim and suggested the effect may only be a wal_consistency_checking failure.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Also, having code that has no users in tree also makes it more likely to bit-rot.

precedents_retrieved.title: heap_insert() and heap_update() optimization
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reduced repeated BufferGetPage(buffer) calls inside heap_insert() and heap_update() to make these functions faster. The author reported speedups of about 5.6% for heap_insert() and 11.4% for heap_update() in an optimized build.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author repeated the timing tests and found no real gain: the patched build averaged 1303 against 1272 for the original. He suggested that autovacuum, analyze or a checkpoint may have affected the first run. Andres Freund had said the first numbers looked large and suggested checking the generated code. The thread ends there, and the entry was rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: However I've just done some extra time tests and didn't notice so significant difference as early.

precedents_retrieved.title: Refactor how we form HeapTuples for CatalogTuple(Insert|Update)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds macros in htup.h and a heap_update_tuple() function so that catalog code records the columns it changes in a Bitmapset and passes it to CatalogTupleUpdate(). simple_heap_update() then uses that set instead of calling HeapDetermineColumnsInfo() under the page lock, and the patch converts nearly all catalog update call sites.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund asked whether avoiding some comparisons during catalog changes was worth this many changes. Tom Lane said a system-wide API change costs a lot of review work, breaks pending patches and extensions, and makes back-patching harder for years, so it would need very large performance gains. He also questioned the switch from bool arrays to a Bitmapset, which adds a palloc. The author agreed the gains would not be large and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: With that in mind, you'd have to show *massive* performance improvements for it to have any chance of getting accepted. Frankly I doubt it can possibly clear that bar.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
Reverted commit(s): VACUUM: ignore indexing operations with CONCURRENTLY
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit d9d076222f5b "VACUUM: ignore indexing operations
with CONCURRENTLY".

These changes caused indexes created with the CONCURRENTLY option to
miss heap tuples that were HOT-updated and HOT-pruned during the index
creation.  Before these changes, HOT pruning would have been prevented
by the Xmin of the transaction creating the index, but because this
change was precisely to allow the Xmin to move forward ignoring that
backend, now other backends scanning the table can prune them.  This is
not a problem for VACUUM (which requires a lock that conflicts with a
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY operation), but HOT-prune can definitely
occur.  In other words, Xmin advancement was sped up, but at the cost of
corrupting the resulting index.

Regrettably, this means that the new feature in PG14 that RIC/CIC on
very large tables no longer force VACUUM to retain very old tuples goes
away.  We might try to implement it again in a later release, but for
now the risk of indexes missing tuples is too high and there's no easy
fix.

Backpatch to 14, where this change appeared.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
Reverted commit(s): Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2aa6e33, that added a fast path to skip
anti-wraparound and non-aggressive autovacuum jobs (these have no sense
as anti-wraparound implies aggressive).  With a cluster using a high
amount of relations with a portion of them being heavily updated, this
could cause autovacuum to lock down, with autovacuum workers attempting
repeatedly those jobs on the same relations for the same database, that
just kept being skipped.  This lock down can be solved with a manual
VACUUM FREEZE.

Justin King has reported one environment where the issue happened, and
Julien Rouhaud and I have been able to reproduce it in a second
environment.  With a very aggressive autovacuum_freeze_max_age,
triggering those jobs with pgbench is a matter of minutes, and hitting
the lock down is a lot harder (my local tests failed to do that).

Note that anti-wraparound and non-aggressive jobs can only be triggered
on a subset of shared catalogs:
- pg_auth_members
- pg_authid
- pg_database
- pg_replication_origin
- pg_shseclabel
- pg_subscription
- pg_tablespace
While the lock down was possible down to v12, the root cause of those
jobs is a much older issue, which needs more analysis.

Bonus thanks to Andres Freund for the discussion.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent list has no earlier rejected, returned or reverted attempt at this fix. Message #1 points to a 2022 report on 14.5 with the same error, and the thread presents it as a bug report that this patch resolves, so it gives no rejection reason to apply here. Heikki reviewed the patch and reports in message #9 that it was committed and back-patched.

No standards or compatibility objection applies. The fix adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump content or client-visible protocol change, and its only behaviour changes remove an error and a spurious serialization failure. The new injection point in xact.c is for tests only.

The fix changes only in-memory conflict and status decisions in heapam.c, plus a test-only injection point in xact.c. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol or struct change, so pg_upgrade, standbys, logical decoding and back-branch ABI are not affected. The extra WAL from heap_lock_updated_tuple_rec() on a crashed creator's successor exists today and the patch leaves it as it is. Whether the recovery test with a prepared transaction reached the back branches cannot be checked from the material.

The fix has no privilege or exposure aspect, since it only changes how heap_update and the multixact conflict check treat an aborted or crashed updater. The added wait lasts until ProcArray cleanup, which is a short window that a user cannot extend, and the new injection point in xact.c exists only in builds with injection points enabled.

This is a correctness fix in heapam.c conflict checks, reviewed and committed by Heikki, an engaged committer who knows the area (message #9), with an independent plain-SQL reproducer (message #7). It adds no new mechanism, GUC or API, and the only added waiting is the short window between the pg_xact abort write and ProcArray cleanup. Two points could not be checked without the code or the final commit: which branches received the injection point and tests, and whether heap_lock_updated_tuple_rec() still uses TransactionIdDidAbort(). Message #3 says the author analyzed that function and found no user-visible issue.

This is a correctness fix inside heapam.c for a race in the multixact updater checks. No existing feature, setting, extension or documented workaround avoids the "new multixact has more than one updating member" error or the spurious TM_Updated for crashed updaters. The fix changes existing checks and adds no second mechanism, so the already-exists angle has nothing to object to.

The material shows real demand for this bug fix. There is an independent field report (message #7) with a plain-SQL pgbench reproducer that fails on released 18.1 and 18.4, the author hit it under TPC-C (message #8), and a 2022 report on 14.5 shows the same error (message #1). The fix changes only internal heapam.c behaviour and adds a test-only injection point, so no cost falls on non-users.
